lessons.title: Firebase Project Setup
lessons.content:
# Firebase Project Setup

Firebase is a Backend-as-a-Service platform that bundles authentication, databases, storage, hosting, analytics, and serverless functions under one project.

### Core setup steps
- Create a Firebase project in the console.
- Register your web or mobile app.
- Add the SDK and initialize it with your project config.
- Turn on only the products you actually need.

### Practical rule
Keep Firebase config in one shared module so the rest of the app imports initialized services instead of repeating setup logic.

lessons.title: Authentication Basics
lessons.content:
# Authentication Basics

Firebase Authentication handles sign-in flows such as email/password, Google, GitHub, and anonymous sessions.

### Common concepts
- `createUserWithEmailAndPassword` creates accounts.
- `signInWithEmailAndPassword` signs in existing users.
- `onAuthStateChanged` reacts to login state changes.
- Security rules should assume the client is untrusted.

### Good practice
Drive UI state from the authenticated user object and keep route guards separate from visual components.

lessons.title: Firestore Documents and Collections
lessons.content:
# Firestore Documents and Collections

Cloud Firestore stores data in collections, documents, and nested subcollections.

### Model basics
- A collection contains documents.
- A document stores fields as key-value pairs.
- Reads are usually scoped to a document or query.
- Writes use `setDoc`, `addDoc`, `updateDoc`, or `deleteDoc`.

### Design tip
Model data around access patterns. If a screen needs to query by owner and status, store those fields explicitly instead of reconstructing them later.

lessons.title: Realtime Reads and Queries
lessons.content:
# Realtime Reads and Queries

Firestore supports one-time reads and realtime subscriptions.

### Main APIs
- `getDoc` and `getDocs` fetch once.
- `onSnapshot` subscribes to changes.
- `query`, `where`, `orderBy`, and `limit` build filtered reads.

### Performance note
Subscribe only where realtime behavior matters. Dashboards, notifications, and collaborative views are good candidates; static profile data usually is not.

lessons.title: Cloud Storage and File Uploads
lessons.content:
# Cloud Storage and File Uploads

Firebase Storage is used for user uploads such as avatars, PDFs, and media files.

### Typical flow
1. Create a storage reference.
2. Upload with `uploadBytes` or `uploadBytesResumable`.
3. Fetch a public download URL when needed.
4. Store file metadata in Firestore if the app needs querying.

### Security tip
Do not rely on file names for authorization. Use storage rules and paths tied to authenticated user or tenant identifiers.

lessons.title: Cloud Functions Overview
lessons.content:
# Cloud Functions Overview

Cloud Functions let you run backend code without managing servers.

### Common uses
- React to Firestore writes.
- Send notifications or emails.
- Create secure callable APIs.
- Process uploads after they land in storage.

### Design rule
Use Functions for privileged operations that should not run in the client, especially anything involving secrets, admin access, or system-wide side effects.

lessons.title: Security Rules Essentials
lessons.content:
# Security Rules Essentials

Firebase security rules control who can read or write data in Firestore and Storage.

### Important ideas
- Rules are not filters; queries must already satisfy them.
- Validate both authentication and document shape.
- Check ownership, membership, or role fields explicitly.
- Deny by default and open only what is necessary.

### Review habit
Test rules with both allowed and denied cases before shipping schema changes.

lessons.title: Environment Configuration and Deployment
lessons.content:
# Environment Configuration and Deployment

A production Firebase app usually has separate environments for local work, staging, and production.

### Checklist
- Keep client config in environment variables where appropriate.
- Use separate Firebase projects for risky experiments.
- Review indexes, rules, and function configs during deployment.
- Track which app points to which backend.

### Operational tip
Most Firebase incidents come from pointing the wrong frontend at the wrong project or deploying loose security rules.

lessons.title: Debugging Firebase Apps
lessons.content:
# Debugging Firebase Apps

Firebase issues usually come from configuration mismatches, missing indexes, or rejected security rules.

### Fast debugging path
- Confirm the current project ID.
- Check browser console and network responses.
- Read Firestore or Storage rule errors closely.
- Verify the authenticated user and expected document path.

### Team rule
When a Firebase error appears, capture the exact failing operation and path first. Vague "read failed" reports slow down debugging.
